reference_title: Pavement Design for Roads, Streets, Walks, and Storage Areas

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.summary: This UFC provides minimum criteria for the design procedures and requirements for pavement design of roads and parking areas; it clarifies when a State pavement design procedure may be used versus when PCASE is mandatory.
sections.body: This UFC provides minimum criteria for the design procedures and requirements for the pavement design of roads and parking areas. It clarifies when State pavement design procedures may be used and when Pavement-Transportation Computer Assisted Structural Engineering (PCASE) is required. Pavement design engineers must use this minimum criteria when making decisions and determining an acceptable pavement design procedure.
key_points: Covers roads, streets, walks, and open storage areas -- NOT airfields (airfields are UFC 3-260-02).
Clarifies when a State DoT pavement design procedure may substitute for the UFC's own criteria.
PCASE is the mandatory design tool for special military vehicles, non-US locations, and organizational vehicle parking areas.
sections.applicability: Applies whenever a road, street, walk, or storage-area pavement design decision must be made under this UFC.

sections.title: Applicability
sections.summary: This UFC applies to all military service elements and contractors involved in the planning, design, and construction of DoD facilities worldwide.
sections.body: This UFC applies to all military service elements and contractors involved in the planning, design, and construction of DoD facilities worldwide.
key_points: Applies DoD-wide, to all service elements and contractors.
Applies to planning, design, and construction phases.
sections.applicability: Any DoD facility project (military or contractor-executed) worldwide.

sections.title: General Building Requirements
sections.summary: Comply with UFC 1-200-01 (DoD Building Code) in addition to this UFC; UFC 1-200-01 sets applicability of model building codes and government-unique criteria across design disciplines.
sections.body: Comply with UFC 1-200-01, DoD Building Code (General Building Requirements). UFC 1-200-01 provides applicability of model building codes and government unique criteria for typical design disciplines and building systems, as well as for accessibility, antiterrorism, security, high performance and sustainability requirements, and safety. Use this UFC in addition to UFC 1-200-01 and the UFCs and government criteria referenced therein.
key_points: UFC 1-200-01 governs general building-code applicability across disciplines.
This UFC is used IN ADDITION TO, not instead of, UFC 1-200-01.
sections.applicability: All projects governed by this UFC also carry UFC 1-200-01 obligations.

sections.title: References
sections.summary: Appendix A lists the references used in this document; publication dates are intentionally omitted so the latest available issuance of each reference applies.
sections.body: Appendix A contains a list of references used in this document. The publication date of the code or standard is not included in this document. In general, the latest available issuance of the reference is used.
key_points: Appendix A is the master reference list (UFC 3-201-01, UFC 3-250-03/04/11, UFC 3-260-02/03, AASHTO, ASTM, etc.).
No publication dates given -- always use the latest issuance of a referenced standard.
sections.applicability: When resolving which edition of a cited standard governs a design decision.

sections.title: Glossary
sections.summary: Appendix C contains acronyms, USCS soil types, units of measure, definitions of terms, and referenced construction-detail figures.
sections.body: Appendix C contains acronyms, Unified Soil Classification System (USCS) soil types, units of measure, definition of terms and referenced figures.
key_points: Appendix C is the glossary/acronym/USCS/units reference.
Appendix C also carries the Tri-Service pavement construction-detail figures (joints, subdrains).
sections.applicability: When a term, acronym, or construction detail figure needs to be looked up.
